nodes.label: Task Residual Spectrum (TRS)
nodes.rationale: Departure of LoRA B-matrix singular values from Marchenko-Pastur null distribution. Architecture-agnostic because MP depends only on matrix aspect ratio, GL_r-invariant because singular values are coordinate-free. Statistically optimal by spiked RMT: computing TRS = computing maximum likelihood estimate of task-specific information.

nodes.label: Intruder Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Above-MP, unaligned singular vectors in LoRA B matrix. Spearman rho=0.97 correlation with catastrophic forgetting. Not correlated with task performance (rho=-0.34). Appear when LoRA is forced out of minor subspace of W_0 by rank constraint — the holonomy accumulated by low-rank constraint.

nodes.label: Universal Weight Subspace
nodes.rationale: 500+ Mistral-7B LoRAs converge to shared 16-dim spectral subspace (arXiv:2512.05117, Theorem 2.5, rate O(1/sqrt(T))). Represents architecture-specific prior for LoRA adaptation. Two-level TRS: departure from MP (remove noise) then departure from universal subspace (remove architecture prior).

nodes.label: Genuine TRS
nodes.rationale: Above-MP, pre-trained aligned, outside universal subspace. The task-specific signal that predicts downstream task performance. Defined as: sigma_i > sigma_MP AND cos(u_i, U_0) > tau_align AND cos(u_i, U_universal) < tau_universal.

nodes.label: Near-zero Suppression Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Near-zero singular values of delta-W encode deliberate capability suppression. Distinct from near-zero of W_0 (minor subspace = free space). Predicts capability loss.

nodes.label: MP Bulk
nodes.rationale: Within-MP singular values — noise or task-general domain adaptation. Subspace-Boosted (2506.16506) proves mathematically that MP null = limit of common LoRA subspace as N→inf. Common subspace singular values stay at O(1) under averaging.

nodes.label: Four-Way Spectral Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Complete theory: delta-W decomposes into (1) Genuine TRS (above-MP, aligned, non-universal), (2) Intruder Dims (above-MP, unaligned), (3) Universal/Task-General (above-MP, aligned, in universal subspace), (4) Suppression Dims (near-zero). Approximately orthogonal for large models (>7B). Each component additively contributes to distinct behavioral outcomes.

nodes.label: Fiber Bundle Structure of Weight Space
nodes.rationale: Weight space as principal bundle P=W with base W/G (symmetry-reduced). Vertical subbundle = G-orbit tangent vectors (pure symmetry). Horizontal = Fisher metric complement (real changes). Connection 1-form = Fisher metric projection to vertical. Confirmed literature gap: no paper simultaneously constructs this full framework.

nodes.label: Fisher Metric Connection
nodes.rationale: Connection 1-form on weight space principal bundle defined by Fisher metric projection. Curvature Omega = domega + [omega,omega] measures non-commutativity of independent moves. Fisher information is approximately architecture-agnostic via Platonic hypothesis.

nodes.label: Holonomy as Task Interference Measure
nodes.rationale: Holonomy around training loop T1->T2->(-T2) != 0 means sequential fine-tuning is irreversible. Intruder dimensions = holonomy accumulated by low-rank constraint. As rank->inf, constraint disappears, holonomy->0, intruders->0. Explains why intruders vanish at high rank.

nodes.label: Weight Disentanglement via TRS Orthogonality
nodes.rationale: Orthogonality condition between TRS components enables zero task interference. OSRM confirms: orthogonal B-subspaces = zero task interference. TRS distance = principal angle between task gradient subspaces = predictor of catastrophic forgetting.

nodes.label: Forgetting Geometry Theorem
nodes.rationale: From Steele (arXiv:2603.02224): forgetting governed by minimum principal angle between gradient subspaces. TRS distance approximates this principal angle. Tasks with similar TRS (small TRS distance) will have overlapping gradient subspaces -> high forgetting.

nodes.label: MiLoRA Paradox and Resolution
nodes.rationale: MiLoRA uses minor (near-zero) SVs of W_0 (free space) for fine-tuning. Apparent contradiction: TRS suppression dims are near-zero of delta-W. Resolution: W_0 minor subspace != delta-W near-zero subspace. Best LoRA occupies minor subspace of W_0; intruder dims appear when LoRA spills from minor into principal subspace of W_0.

nodes.label: Platonic Weight Space Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: From arXiv:2405.07987. Representations converge toward shared statistical model as models scale. Fisher matrices converge across architectures. Enables cross-architecture TRS comparison without alignment. Supports NTK prediction that optimal LoRA subspace is approximately shared.

nodes.label: Spectral-Population Duality
nodes.rationale: Individual TRS (task-specific signal, decays O(1/sqrt(N)) under averaging) vs population PCA (common subspace, stays O(1)). Subspace-Boosted proves mathematically these are complementary: common subspace = MP null limit, TRS = exactly what averaging destroys.

nodes.label: Canonical TRS via QR+SVD
nodes.rationale: Naive SVD of B has infinite factorization ambiguity. W2T (2603.15990): QR decomposition of B then SVD of R gives canonical unique representation. Canonical TRS = log(sigma_i(R) / lambda_MP_edge). Resolves factorization ambiguity for reliable cross-architecture comparison.

nodes.label: TRS as Optimal Bayes Estimator
nodes.rationale: Spiked RMT paper (2410.18938): optimal Bayes estimator of learned signal = Marchenko-Pastur shrinkage. Computing TRS = computing maximum likelihood estimate of task-specific information. TRS >= any other spectral fingerprint in task information content by Gauss-Markov theorem.

nodes.label: 2D Layer Selection Map (alpha x TRS)
nodes.rationale: AlphaLoRA alpha (base model training quality) x TRS (task adaptation strength). Gold layers: high alpha + high TRS. Dormant: high alpha + low TRS. Rescued: low alpha + high TRS (LoRA compensated bad base training). Noise: low alpha + low TRS. No paper has proposed this 2D criterion.

nodes.label: TRS_HTMP Next-Generation Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Standard MP is wrong null for trained networks. HTMP (2506.03470) parameterized by kappa (eigenvalue repulsion). TRS_HTMP = departure from HTMP null = purely task-specific (no training artifact). 2D task fingerprint: (kappa, TRS_HTMP) = task component count + task signal strength.

nodes.label: TRS-based Continual Learning Curriculum
nodes.rationale: Find task ordering maximizing minimum pairwise TRS distance between consecutive tasks -> minimizes catastrophic forgetting. Equivalent to maximum weight Hamiltonian path on TRS distance graph. Greedy: always pick task with maximum TRS distance from current task.

nodes.label: Zero-Shot LoRA Audit via LoL + TRS
nodes.rationale: LoL paradigm (2410.04207) shows task properties learnable from LoRA weights. TRS is canonical GL_r-invariant feature for LoL. Protocol: given any LoRA checkpoint, compute canonical TRS, run LoL meta-prediction, output: task label, training data characteristics, performance estimate, harmful fine-tune detection.

nodes.label: Bayesian Spectral Calibration Unification
nodes.rationale: TRS (MP null) and SVC (Singular Value Calibration) are special cases of Bayesian spectral calibration. Hierarchy: MP null subset universal subspace null subset empirical shared null. MP null = maximum entropy prior, most generalizable (works any architecture, any task distribution).

nodes.label: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning Intruder Dimensions (2410.21228)
No Task Left Behind Isotropic Merging (2502.04959)
D2C Data-Driven Adapter Clustering and Merging (2601.17441)
nodes.author: Bohdal et al.

nodes.label: SVD Features for LoRA Clustering
nodes.rationale: K-Means w/ SVD clustering uses cosine similarities of SVD features extracted from LoRAs. Clusters are predominantly by task (not language). Task-homogeneous clusters achieve stronger merging performance. Empirical confirmation that SVD features encode task identity.

nodes.label: D2C Iterative Clustering Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Iterative data-driven clustering with n=10 examples per task. Outperforms random/K-Means by 2.1-4.5%. On-device LLM deployment under 12.5% storage budget. Agnostic to merging technique (TIES or linear).

nodes.label: DSiRe Dataset Size Recovery from LoRA (2406.19395)
nodes.author: Salama et al., Hebrew University

nodes.label: LoRA Spectrum Encodes Dataset Size
nodes.rationale: Frobenius norm of LoRA matrices negatively correlated with fine-tuning dataset size (models overfit faster on smaller datasets). Singular values more discriminative than scalar Frobenius norm. Layer-wise spectra vary: up layers more discriminative than down layers. NTK prediction: effective rank ~ sqrt(N) connects directly.

nodes.label: Spectral Imbalance in LoRA Updates
nodes.rationale: LoRA update matrices exhibit long-tailed singular value spectra: few dominant components absorb most adaptation energy. Imbalanced updates: (i) more likely to disrupt pre-trained knowledge, (ii) more vulnerable to interference from subsequent tasks. Variance of singular values increases throughout training.

nodes.label: Stiefel Manifold Optimization for Balanced LoRA
nodes.rationale: EBLoRA factorizes delta-W_t = s_t U_t V_t^T, decoupling magnitude (s_t) from directional structure (U_t, V_t orthonormal on Stiefel manifold). Explicit balance among rank-one components. Maximally isotropic LoRA: all singular values equal to 1 before s_t scaling. TRS of standard LoRA = distance from Stiefel manifold in spectral space.

nodes.label: Gradient Orthogonality Constraint (EBLoRA)
nodes.rationale: G_{t-1}^T U_t = 0 prevents new task from allocating update directions along previously sensitive gradient modes. Combined with energy balancing achieves MFN 72.8%, BWT -2.0, FWT 34.6% on UCIT benchmark, outperforming all baselines.

nodes.label: EigenLoRAx Task-Invariant Principal Subspace
nodes.rationale: Recycles pretrained LoRAs to extract top-K principal components via SVD/PCA of stacked LoRA weight matrices. Task-specific weights lie within shared principal subspace. 100x fewer parameters than LoRA, 2x faster convergence. Direct application of Universal Weight Subspace Hypothesis. Top-16 PCs contain most information from 4000+ components for 500 LoRAs.

nodes.label: EigenLoRAx Generalization Bound Theorem 3.6
nodes.rationale: Risk bound: ||W*_{d+1} - W_{d+1}||_F^2 <= C1*(sqrt(K)/sqrt(s_t)) + C2. Upper bound tighter when new task lies in shared principal subspace. Rademacher complexity of low-rank class H_{W_E} bounded by O(sqrt(K)||W_E||_F / sqrt(s_t)).

nodes.label: From Spikes to Heavy Tails Spectral Evolution (2406.04657)
nodes.author: Kothapalli et al., NYU/Dartmouth

nodes.label: MP to Spike to Heavy-Tail ESD Pathway
nodes.rationale: ESD evolves: MP (random init) -> Bulk+Spike (one large-eta step) -> Bulk-Decay -> Heavy-Tailed. Spike aligned with task direction beta*. Spectral gap determines HT emergence speed. FB-Adam needs much smaller eta than GD for spike (eta=1 sufficient for FB-Adam vs eta=2000 for GD). PL_alpha in range (2, 2.5) correlates with good generalization. Spike emerges at threshold Theta(1/sqrt(h)) for FB-Adam.

nodes.label: Spectral Maturity Cross-Architecture Confound
nodes.rationale: Spike emergence threshold scales as Theta(1/sqrt(h)) for FB-Adam. Wider architectures (larger h) need larger eta to create spikes. Cross-architecture TRS comparison must control for spectral maturity (whether Bulk+Spike transition occurred). Fix: TRS/PL_Alpha = phase-normalized spectral fingerprint.

nodes.label: GeLoRA Geometric Adaptive Ranks Intrinsic Dim (2412.09250)
nodes.author: Ed-dib et al., NYU/Nace.AI

nodes.label: GeLoRA Rank Bound Theorem 3.2
nodes.rationale: Theorem: LoRA rank r_i >= max(d_{i+1} - d_i, 0), where d_i is intrinsic dimension of data manifold at input of block i. Minimum TRS effective rank = intrinsic dimensionality expansion between consecutive blocks. Architecture-agnostic: same task -> similar d_i profile -> similar TRS rank profile across architectures.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Dimensionality Profile Across Layers
nodes.rationale: Two-nearest-neighbors (TwoNN) method estimates intrinsic dimension d_i at each transformer block. Intrinsic dimensions vary by task and layer. Conjecture 3.1: gap between intrinsic dimension and transformer rank decreases as fine-tuning progresses (TRS compression curve = TRS decreases with training, reflecting generalization).

nodes.label: mtLoRA: Spectral Multitask Regularization for LoRA
nodes.key_contribution: Three novel LoRA designs: spectral-aware regularization, fine-grained routing, block-level adaptation. Achieves 64.0% avg vs HydraLoRA 61.7% with 47% fewer parameters.

nodes.label: RMT Analysis of Feature Learning in Two-Layer NNs (Spiked SRFM)
nodes.key_contribution: Proves spiked SRFM approximation W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta. Derives deterministic equivalent for feature covariance. Proves exact generalization error formula (Theorem 4.8). Feature learning creates heavier tails → better generalization.

nodes.label: SANE: Scalable and Versatile Weight Space Learning
nodes.key_contribution: Sequential Autoencoder for Neural Embeddings. Tokenizes weights layer-wise into windows. Scales to ResNet-18 (~12M params). Outperforms hyper-representations by 25% for zero-shot initialization.

nodes.label: Subspace-Boosted Model Merging via HO-GSVD
nodes.key_contribution: Identifies rank collapse: task-specific SVs decay O(1/sqrt(N)). Proposes Subspace Boosting (clamp small SVs above beta threshold). Introduces HO-GSVD alignment matrix for task similarity.

nodes.label: Gradient Space LoRA: Task Discovery via SVD
nodes.key_contribution: Analyzes gradient space of LoRA through SVD lens to discover task-relevant directions. Links gradient space structure to task residual spectrum.

nodes.label: Heavy-Tailed Mechanistic Universality (HTMP)
nodes.key_contribution: HTMP as improved null distribution over standard Marchenko-Pastur for weight matrices. Heavy-tailed correction accounts for non-Gaussian weight statistics in real neural networks.

nodes.label: Deep Synthesis Night Run 1: Hidden Geometry of Weight Space
nodes.key_contribution: Identifies TRS theory as incomplete; proposes eight frameworks: four-way decomposition, fiber bundle, spectral-population duality, knowledge region as TRS manifold, weight disentanglement = TRS orthogonality, near-zero SVs as anti-tasks, model stitching as TRS test, TRS as sufficient statistic, platonic weight space hypothesis.

nodes.label: New Papers Found: Night Run May 2026
nodes.key_contribution: Catalog of 16 new papers supporting and extending TRS theory across 8 thematic categories.

nodes.label: Four-Way Spectral Decomposition of LoRA
nodes.description: The singular value spectrum of DeltaW decomposes into four functionally distinct regions: (1) True TRS (above-MP, aligned with pre-trained SVs = task signal), (2) Intruder Dimensions (above-MP, NOT aligned = catastrophic forgetting), (3) MP Bulk (within Marchenko-Pastur = domain adaptation), (4) Near-Zero Suppression (below lower MP threshold = capability suppression, not noise).
nodes.formal: TRS_refined(B) = {u_i : sigma_i > sigma_MP_upper AND cos(u_i, V_pretrained) > tau_align}
nodes.rationale: Extends existing TRS framework which only distinguished above-MP vs below-MP. Incorporating alignment criterion separates task signal from forgetting artifacts.

nodes.label: True TRS (Task Residual Spectrum, Refined)
nodes.description: Singular vectors above Marchenko-Pastur upper bound AND aligned with pre-trained singular vectors. Represents genuine task acquisition signal. Predicts task-specific performance improvement.
nodes.formal: TRS_+ = {u_i : sigma_i > sigma_MP_upper AND cos(u_i, V_pretrained) > tau_align}
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes true task signal from intruder dimensions by adding the alignment criterion to the above-MP condition.

nodes.label: Intruder Dimensions
nodes.description: High-magnitude singular vectors in fine-tuned LoRA that are DISSIMILAR to pre-trained singular vectors. Concentrate catastrophic forgetting artifacts. Suppressing them largely restores base model knowledge.
nodes.formal: intruder_score(LoRA) = ||{sigma_i above-MP, not aligned with V_pretrained}||
nodes.rationale: Current TRS includes intruder dimensions by mistake; they predict forgetting, not task performance.

nodes.label: Marchenko-Pastur Bulk (MP Bulk)
nodes.description: Singular values within the Marchenko-Pastur distribution. Encodes domain adaptation / common subspace information. Preserved by averaging (proved by Subspace-Boosted Merging). Not task-specific but not pure noise either.
nodes.rationale: MP bulk is the third region of the four-way decomposition; it carries distribution-level information rather than task-specific information.

nodes.label: Near-Zero Singular Values as Anti-Tasks (TRS_-)
nodes.description: Singular vectors below the lower MP threshold. NOT noise — structured capability suppression. Removing them causes outsized performance collapse. Fine-tuning deliberately suppresses certain capabilities to specialize.
nodes.formal: TRS_- = {singular vectors with sigma < sigma_MP_lower, sigma > 0} = capabilities SUPPRESSED
nodes.application: Forgetting diagnosis: if TRS_-(T1) intersect TRS_+(T2) != empty, then training on T1 will catastrophically forget T2.
nodes.rationale: Fourth region of decomposition; capability suppression creates the specialization signature of fine-tuning.

nodes.label: Rank Collapse in Model Merging
nodes.description: When merging N task vectors via Task Arithmetic, task-specific singular values decay O(1/sqrt(N)) while common subspace SVs remain O(1). Stable rank collapses to stable rank of common subspace only.
propositions: Prop 2: stable rank collapses to common subspace stable rank
nodes.rationale: Explains why naive averaging destroys task-specific information and motivates subspace boosting.

nodes.label: Subspace Boosting Algorithm
nodes.description: SVD-based mitigation of rank collapse. Clamps small singular values above a beta threshold to preserve task-specific subspace structure during model merging.
nodes.pseudocode: U, S, Vh = svd(param); c_sum = torch.cumsum(S); k = (n_sum >= beta).nonzero(); S_new = torch.clamp(S, S[idx]); new_param = U @ diag(S_new) @ Vh
nodes.rationale: Directly counteracts O(1/sqrt(N)) SV decay by enforcing minimum singular value magnitude.

nodes.label: HO-GSVD (Higher-Order Generalized SVD) for Task Similarity
nodes.description: Decomposes N task vectors into distinct U_i Sigma_i and shared V subspace: A_i = U_i Sigma_i V^T where V is shared. Alignment Matrix A_{ij} = (1/L) sum_l (1/M_l) sum_p |log(sigma^(l)_{i,p} / sigma^(l)_{j,p})| measures task similarity.
nodes.formal: A_i = U_i Sigma_i V^T, V in R^{n x n} shared across all tasks
nodes.rationale: Enables principled comparison of task subspaces across multiple models by factoring out the shared basis.

nodes.label: Spectral-Aware Regularization (mtLoRA)
nodes.description: Selectively orthogonalizes only low-SV components of LoRA matrices across tasks. Uses weight w(sigma) = exp(-sigma/sigma_bar) so that high-SV (shared knowledge) components are preserved while low-SV (task-specific) components are orthogonalized.
nodes.formal: L_spectral = lambda * sum_{i<j} ||(B'_i)^T B'_j||^2_F, where B' is SV-weighted
nodes.empirical_finding: High-SV top-20% components have 89% inter-task alignment; bottom 50% have only 3%.
nodes.rationale: Exploits the empirical observation that high-SV components are shared across tasks while low-SV components are task-specific.

nodes.label: Block-Level Adaptation (mtLoRA)
nodes.description: LoRA as parallel path bypassing attention/FFN non-linearities. Reduces gradient conflict from -0.054 to -0.013 cosine similarity across tasks.
nodes.rationale: Non-linearities introduce gradient conflicts in multitask learning; bypassing them with LoRA parallel paths reduces inter-task interference.

nodes.label: Fine-Grained Routing (mtLoRA)
nodes.description: Dimension-specific MLP router producing weight vectors Pi_i in R^g for g groups. Routes task-specific information to appropriate LoRA dimensions at fine granularity.
nodes.rationale: Coarser task-level routing (e.g., MoE per layer) wastes capacity; dimension-level routing allows more precise task specialization.

nodes.label: Spiked RMT / SRFM (Spiked Random Feature Model)
nodes.description: Weight matrix after one gradient step: W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta, where spike v is correlated with target direction w*. Proved via deterministic equivalent of feature covariance matrix.
nodes.formal: W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta; spike v correlated with w*
nodes.theorem: Theorem 4.8: exact generalization error formula derivable from spiked SRFM approximation
nodes.rationale: Provides theoretical grounding for why feature learning (not just lazy/NTK regime) creates above-MP singular value spikes.

nodes.label: Deterministic Equivalent for Feature Covariance
nodes.description: RMT technique that replaces stochastic feature covariance matrix with a deterministic approximation that captures the same spectral statistics. Used to prove exact generalization error in the spiked SRFM setting.
nodes.rationale: Enables rigorous theoretical analysis of feature learning without requiring independence assumptions that fail in practice.

nodes.label: Hyper-Representations via SANE
nodes.description: Task-agnostic latent space embeddings of neural network weights. SANE encodes weight sequences into embeddings that correlate with WeightWatcher metrics and model accuracy. Scales 3 orders of magnitude beyond previous hyper-representation methods.
nodes.rationale: Task-agnostic training enables generalization across model architectures and tasks; sequential tokenization preserves layer-wise structure.

nodes.label: Weight Tokenization (SANE)
nodes.description: Tokenizes NN weight sequences into windows of size ws. Each token = weight window from a layer. Enables transformer encoder to process weights of arbitrary architectures sequentially.
nodes.formal: Input: weight matrices M_{s,n}, tokenized into windows; Loss: L_rec = ||M_{s,n} odot (T_{s,n} - T_hat_{s,n})||^2 + L_c (NTXent contrastive)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-window tokenization allows SANE to handle variable-size networks without architecture-specific preprocessing.

nodes.label: Fiber Bundle Framework for Weight Space
nodes.description: Neural network weight space W as a fiber bundle. Total space W = R^d. Base space T = task manifold (parameterized by TRS_refined directions). Fiber F_w = {w' : TRS_refined(w') = TRS_refined(w)} = G-symmetry equivalence class. Projection pi(w) = TRS_refined(w). Structure group G = permutation symmetry group.
nodes.connection: Connection 1-form = Fisher Information Matrix restricted to task directions.
nodes.explanatory_power: Weight alignment NP-hard = different sections of fiber bundle; task arithmetic works = addition in base space T; merging fails = holonomy; mode connectivity = paths in T lifting to W.
nodes.rationale: Provides a unified geometric framework that explains all existing model composition methods as special cases.

nodes.label: Holonomy as Task Interference
nodes.description: Curvature of the fiber bundle connection encodes interference between tasks. If two task vectors tau_1, tau_2 have non-zero holonomy, then task arithmetic fails for them. This is precisely the disentanglement error xi(alpha_1, alpha_2) from Ortiz-Jiménez et al.
nodes.formal: Non-zero holonomy(tau_1, tau_2) <=> task arithmetic fails for (tau_1, tau_2)
nodes.rationale: Holonomy formalizes why task composition sometimes fails: going around a loop in task manifold T doesn't return to same fiber point.

nodes.label: Weight Disentanglement = TRS Orthogonality
nodes.description: Two task vectors tau_1, tau_2 are weight-disentangled iff their TRS_refined subspaces are orthogonal in the Grassmannian sense: d_Grassmannian(TRS_refined(tau_1), TRS_refined(tau_2)) ≈ 1 (= pi/2 principal angle).
nodes.prediction: For random init models: d_Grassmannian non-orthogonal. For pre-trained models: d_Grassmannian ≈ 1. Matches empirical finding that task arithmetic is emergent property of pre-training.
nodes.rationale: Pre-training induces NTK eigenfunctions that localize to task domains, producing nearly orthogonal TRS directions for different tasks.

nodes.label: Spectral-Population Duality
nodes.description: The k-th principal component of population-level PCA = linear combination of TRS vectors across individual LoRAs: PC_k = sum_i alpha_{ik} * TRS_i(B_i). w2w space = space spanned by TRS vectors across population. Hyper-representations = encodings converging to TRS-based features.
nodes.prediction: Cosine similarity between PC_k of w2w and average TRS_k across models should be r > 0.7.
nodes.rationale: PCA on a population of LoRAs is an efficient approximation of TRS; this explains WHY population-level PCA works.

nodes.label: Platonic Weight Space Hypothesis
nodes.description: As models scale, weight space structure converges to a canonical form. NTK eigenfunctions become increasingly localized. Spectral structure approaches universal Marchenko-Pastur + task spikes form. TRS directions for same task become increasingly aligned across architectures.
nodes.prediction: For larger models (GPT-4, Llama-3-70B), TRS cross-architecture alignment higher than for smaller models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B).
nodes.analogy: Weight-space analog of Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al., ICML 2024).
nodes.rationale: Scale drives convergence of representational geometry; this should manifest in weight space as well as activation space.

nodes.label: Marchenko-Pastur Distribution
nodes.description: Standard null hypothesis for random weight matrices. Describes the expected singular value distribution of a random Gaussian matrix. Deviations above upper bound = signal; deviations below lower bound = suppression (not noise per Staats et al.).
nodes.rationale: Provides the null against which task-relevant spectral deviations are measured.

nodes.label: Grassmannian Distance for Subspace Comparison
nodes.description: Proper metric for comparing task subspaces via principal angles between subspaces, not cosine similarity of individual vectors. Critical for cross-architecture TRS comparison and weight disentanglement measurement.
nodes.rationale: Individual vector cosine similarity is inadequate for comparing subspaces; principal angles capture the full geometric relationship between subspaces.

nodes.label: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Vectors Adaptation
nodes.key_contribution: Initializes LoRA with principal singular components of pre-trained weights. Outperforms standard LoRA across 12 models, 13 tasks. Operational complement of TRS.

nodes.label: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: Intruder Dimensions (Shuttleworth et al.)
nodes.key_contribution: Introduces intruder dimensions: high-magnitude SVs in LoRA DISSIMILAR to pre-trained SVs. Suppressing them largely restores base model knowledge.

nodes.label: Small Singular Values Matter: RMT Analysis of Transformer Models (Staats et al.)
nodes.key_contribution: Uses MP as null; finds deviations at BOTH top AND bottom of spectrum are task-relevant. Removing small (near-zero) SVs post-fine-tuning causes outsized performance collapse.

nodes.label: Universal Weight Subspace Hypothesis
nodes.key_contribution: Analyzes 1,100+ models (500 Mistral-7B LoRAs, 500 ViTs, 50 LLaMA-8B). Diverse tasks concentrate weight updates in SHARED low-dimensional spectral subspaces. Directly corroborates TRS universality.

nodes.label: Learning in the Fisher Subspace: Guided Initialization for LoRA
nodes.key_contribution: Uses Fisher information matrix to identify task-relevant directions for LoRA initialization. Bridges Fisher geometry and LoRA singular value spectrum directly.

nodes.label: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime Has No Spurious Local Minima
nodes.key_contribution: Proves full fine-tuning admits low-rank solution of rank ~sqrt(N). LoRA with rank > sqrt(N) eliminates all spurious local minima. First formal guarantee that LoRA's restricted movement is sufficient.

nodes.label: Geometry of Neural Net Parameter Spaces Under Reparametrization (Kristiadi et al.)
nodes.key_contribution: Proves Fisher information metric is 'always present' and cannot be removed. Euclidean Hessian measures of flatness are coordinate-dependent. Riemannian foundation for why singular directions are geometrically privileged.

nodes.label: Physics-Inspired Singular Learning Theory to Understand Grokking
nodes.key_contribution: Applies Watanabe's RLCT to predict phase transitions. SLT implies MP bulk = degenerate (uninformative) singular model. Transitions ABOVE bulk signal change in geometric complexity.

nodes.label: Compressibility Measures Complexity: MDL Meets SLT
nodes.key_contribution: MDL principle to singular models via SLT. LLC (local learning coefficient) = geometric invariant of loss landscape. Linearly correlated with compressibility across quantization and factorization.

nodes.label: Bilinear MLPs Enable Weight-Based Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.key_contribution: Bilinear MLPs expressible as linear operations via third-order tensor. Eigendecomposition of weights → interpretable low-rank structure. Recover circuits directly from weight matrices.

nodes.label: Interpretability in Parameter Space: APD (Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition)
nodes.key_contribution: Decomposes network weights into mechanistic components. Faithful, minimal, maximally simple decomposition. Parameters-first approach bridging MDL and mechanistic interpretability.

nodes.label: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations (Bansal et al.)
nodes.key_contribution: Model stitching as stronger probe than CKA. Operational meaning: whether one model's geometry is usable by another. TRS cross-architecture universality can be tested via stitching.

nodes.label: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
nodes.key_contribution: Winning tickets = stable to SGD noise in weight space. Connects LMC geometry to subnetwork trainability.

nodes.label: Approaching Deep Learning through the Spectral Dynamics of Weights
nodes.key_contribution: Tracks SVD of weight matrices throughout training. Unifies grokking, lottery tickets, loss surface structure via spectral evolution. Weight decay acts geometrically to sharpen spectral structure.

nodes.label: The Spectral Lifecycle of Transformer Training
nodes.key_contribution: Tracks full SVD every 25 steps, 30M-285M param models. Discovers transient compression waves propagating depth-wise. Q/K asymmetry vs V in spectral terms. Rank and spectral shape encode fundamentally different training information.

nodes.label: No Task Left Behind: Isotropic Model Merging
nodes.key_contribution: Subspace Alignment Ratio from top SVD singular vectors. Grassmannian of leading singular subspaces as natural metric space for comparing models.

edges.rationale: mtLoRA paper directly introduces spectral-aware regularization as one of its three novel design components.
mtLoRA paper directly introduces block-level adaptation as one of its three novel design components.
mtLoRA paper directly introduces fine-grained routing as one of its three novel design components.
The Dandi et al. paper directly introduces the spiked SRFM (Spiked Random Feature Model) approximation and proves its properties.
The paper derives the deterministic equivalent for feature covariance as a key technical tool.
SANE paper introduces the Sequential Autoencoder for Neural Embeddings and the hyper-representation approach at scale.
SANE paper directly introduces weight tokenization as its core architectural innovation.
Subspace-Boosted Merging paper formally proves rank collapse via Propositions 1-3 with O(1/sqrt(N)) decay result.
Subspace-Boosted Merging paper introduces the Subspace Boosting algorithm as the solution to rank collapse.
Subspace-Boosted Merging paper introduces HO-GSVD and the Alignment Matrix for task similarity measurement.
Shuttleworth et al. directly introduces the concept of intruder dimensions and characterizes their role in catastrophic forgetting.
Staats et al. directly demonstrates that near-zero SVs are not noise: removing them causes outsized performance collapse.
The synthesis document explicitly proposes and formalizes the four-way decomposition as an extension of existing TRS theory.
The synthesis document proposes the fiber bundle framework as Framework 1.
The synthesis document proposes the Spectral-Population Duality as Framework 2.
The synthesis document proposes Weight Disentanglement = TRS Orthogonality as Framework 4.
The synthesis document proposes the Platonic Weight Space Hypothesis as Framework 8.
The synthesis document explicitly claims holonomy encodes task interference within the fiber bundle framework.
True TRS is explicitly Region 1 of the four-way decomposition in the synthesis document.
Intruder Dimensions is explicitly Region 2 of the four-way decomposition.
MP Bulk is explicitly Region 3 of the four-way decomposition.
Near-Zero Suppression is explicitly Region 4 of the four-way decomposition.
Intruder dimensions are defined as above-MP singular values NOT aligned with pre-trained SVs; MP is the reference distribution.
Near-zero SVs are defined as below the lower MP threshold; MP is the reference distribution.
True TRS is defined as above the upper MP threshold AND aligned with pre-trained SVs; MP is the reference distribution.
Holonomy is a standard property of fiber bundles with connections; the synthesis document claims task interference IS holonomy of the fiber bundle connection. This is theoretically sound inference.
The synthesis document explicitly states the connection 1-form is the Fisher Information Matrix; Kristiadi et al. proves FIM is the canonical Riemannian metric on parameter space.
Spectral-aware regularization orthogonalizes low-SV components to reduce inter-task interference; this is operationally equivalent to enforcing TRS orthogonality between tasks at the low-SV end.
Subspace boosting is directly proposed as the solution to the rank collapse problem in the same paper.
Synthesis document states MP bulk is 'preserved by averaging (proved by Subspace-Boosted Merging)'. Subspace boosting enhances this property by clamping small SVs.

Spectral-population duality claims PCA on population of LoRAs finds TRS directions; SANE's hyper-representations also use population-level structure. The duality would explain why SANE embeddings correlate with task-relevant metrics.
The spiked model W^0 + uv^T + Delta extends the basic random matrix (MP bulk) model by adding a structured rank-1 spike; the spiked structure creates deviations from MP.
HTMP is described as an improved null distribution over standard Marchenko-Pastur; it provides a heavy-tailed correction for real neural networks.

PiSSA initializes LoRA with principal singular components of pre-trained weights, which aligns with the true TRS concept of using aligned above-MP singular vectors. Synthesis document calls PiSSA 'operational complement of TRS'.
Universal Weight Subspace Hypothesis (1,100+ models) shows diverse tasks concentrate weight updates in shared low-dimensional spectral subspaces; directly supports TRS universality claim.
Fisher subspace LoRA uses FIM to identify task-relevant directions; FIM is the connection 1-form in the fiber bundle framework. The paper bridges FIM geometry and LoRA SVD spectrum.
Proves LoRA with rank > sqrt(N) has no spurious local minima in NTK regime; provides theoretical justification for spectral regularization being sufficient (not needing full fine-tuning).

Model stitching tests representational compatibility; synthesis document explicitly proposes using stitching as a test of TRS compatibility which is measured by Grassmannian distance between TRS subspaces.

SLT paper implies MP bulk = degenerate (uninformative) singular model in Watanabe's framework; transitions above bulk signal changes in geometric complexity. MP bulk gains theoretical interpretation via SLT.
Isotropic merging paper uses Grassmannian of leading singular subspaces as natural metric space for comparing models; directly employs Grassmannian geometry.
Both HO-GSVD alignment matrix and Grassmannian distance measure relationships between subspaces across multiple models; HO-GSVD uses log-ratio of SVs while Grassmannian uses principal angles.
Weight tokenization is the core mechanism that enables SANE to build hyper-representations at scale; it is the architectural innovation that scales the approach to ResNet-18.
Spectral dynamics paper tracks SVD throughout training and uses MP as reference; it observes how spectral structure evolves relative to the MP bulk.

Spectral lifecycle paper finds Q/K asymmetry and that rank vs spectral shape encode different training information; this supports the four-way decomposition claim that different spectral regions carry fundamentally different information.

Bilinear MLP interpretability via eigendecomposition of weights is a different approach to extracting structure from weight matrices; both approaches agree that low-rank spectral structure in weights = interpretable task information.
APD decomposes network weights into mechanistic components; this 'parameters-first' approach parallels the four-way decomposition's goal of assigning functional meaning to spectral regions.
Platonic weight space hypothesis predicts that TRS directions become more architecture-independent at scale; this implies weight disentanglement (TRS orthogonality) should improve with model scale.

MDL + SLT measures compressibility and geometric complexity (LLC) of loss landscape; near-zero SVs represent a compressible (low LLC) part of the model, potentially interpretable via MDL as structured suppression.
Gradient space LoRA task discovery via SVD is directly related to TRS: TRS identifies task-relevant directions in the weight delta, and gradient-space SVD analysis would find similar structures.

Winning tickets are stable to SGD noise in weight space and exhibit linear mode connectivity; this is consistent with lottery tickets lying on the same fiber (same TRS projection) as the fully trained model.

Both are above-MP singular vectors but distinguished by alignment with pre-trained SVs. True TRS predicts task performance; intruder dimensions predict catastrophic forgetting. Semantically opposite despite spectral similarity.

Both are markers of catastrophic forgetting: intruder dimensions cause forgetting by displacing pre-trained directions; near-zero SVs record what was suppressed. They describe forgetting from complementary perspectives.

Spectral-aware regularization in mtLoRA orthogonalizes low-SV (task-specific) components between tasks; this would reduce the development of intruder dimensions by preventing LoRA matrices from developing task-conflicting high-SV components.
Subspace boosting directly addresses rank collapse; they are two sides of the same phenomenon (problem and solution). The beta threshold in boosting is set to counteract the O(1/sqrt(N)) decay.

HO-GSVD decomposes N task vectors into individual U_i Sigma_i and shared V subspace; spectral-population duality claims population PCA = linear combination of individual TRS vectors. Both formalize how individual and population spectral structure relate.

hyperedges.description: Complete framework describing the four functionally distinct regions of the LoRA singular value spectrum and their roles in task adaptation, forgetting, and capability suppression.
hyperedges.rationale: The four-way decomposition is the central theoretical contribution of this synthesis session, combining insights from Shuttleworth (intruder dims), Staats (near-zero SVs), and the MP literature into a unified framework.

hyperedges.label: Spectral-Population Duality: TRS and Population PCA
hyperedges.description: The proposed equivalence between individual-model TRS vectors and population-level PCA principal components, unifying single-model spectral analysis with population-level weight space learning.
hyperedges.rationale: This duality is a theoretical prediction (not yet validated) connecting the single-model spectral view (TRS) with population-level methods (SANE, HO-GSVD). All participating nodes contribute to or would be explained by this framework.

hyperedges.label: Fiber Bundle Geometric Framework for Weight Space
hyperedges.description: The fiber bundle framework unifying weight space geometry: TRS as base space projection, G-symmetry as fiber structure, Fisher metric as connection, holonomy as task interference. Explains model composition, alignment difficulty, and mode connectivity as geometric phenomena.
hyperedges.rationale: The fiber bundle is the geometric unification framework proposed in the synthesis. All participating nodes are either components of the framework (holonomy, Grassmannian, TRS as base space) or provide theoretical grounding (Fisher geometry papers).
